headline: Statistical models refine causal variant, regulatory, and allelic effect inference
label: Statistical Variant Inference Methods
summary: Bayesian, transfer-learning, and transformer methods are now applied to population-scale genetic data to infer variant-level effects with quantitative…
synthesis: The dominant thread is embedding functional or prior information into statistical inference for variant-level effects, with performance reported against explicit baselines or benchmarks. Genome-wide fine-mapping with functional annotations outperforms locus-by-locus methods in simulations and real data, and KGWAS reports preserved power after pruning its knowledge graph and adding Perturb-seq-derived gene-gene links. GenoBERT reports r² ≈ 0.98 for imputation on LOS and 1000 Genomes, while Bayesian models in two preprints infer rare regulatory mutations from pooled STARR-seq and allelic imbalance inheritance modes from trio ASE and ATAC-seq. Multi-ancestry extensions appear in MRBEE-TL and in a 458-donor monocyte meQTL atlas. What is new is quantitative evaluation of these inference choices across modalities rather than assumption of them. The studies are heterogeneous in scope, and most of the evidence here comes from preprints.
